items.stem: Have you ever had a similar experience, where your parents encouraged you to do something that you were too scared to try ? Discuss this in pairs or group.
items.answer: Yes, I had a similar experience while learning to ride a bicycle in my school days. In my initial attempts, I fell down every time and developed a fear of cycling in my mind which was difficult to overcome. No amount of provoking and cajoling could let me try it again, but my father encouraged me to overcome the fear and helped me as he was adamant about my learning cycling. He took me to a raised, open ground near our house and made me sit, and asked me to put my hands on the handle and feet on the paddle. Since the ground was a slope, I sped down and enjoyed it greatly. This ended my fear and developed my confidence. Thus, I overcame my fear of cycling and started riding a cycle every day.

items.stem: Write a short composition on your initial attempts at learning a skill. You could describe the challenges of learning to ride a bicycle or learning to swim. Make it as humorous as possible.
items.answer: Learning to Ride a Bicycle I learned to ride bicycle when I was ten year old. In my childhood bicycle always fascinated me. I wanted to ride bicycle when I saw other boys going to school on their bicycles. Then my father gave me one as a birthday present. He helped me learn it in my street. But I found it difficult to learn at first. I could not make balance. I could not see ahead as my eyes glued to the paddles. My father told me to see ahead. He held the bicycle from behind. Then one day he left it and I found that I was riding it independently. But I fell down after going a metre away. After that I was always afraid of falling. My father insisted me not to be afraid. I tried. I fell down several times. Finally my fear began to lessen. Now I could ride a few metre without the help of my father. Then I made myself perfect. And the day came when I went to school on bicycle. Indeed, learning to ride bicycle was a wonderful experience.

items.stem: Briefly bring out the contrast between the young seagull’s initial attempts to fly and his first successful flight. Or Compare and contrast the young seagull in the beginning and at the end of the lesson.
items.answer: 2024 The young seagull’s initial attempts to fly were marked by fear and hesitation. He was afraid of the height and the thought of falling. He would flap his wings timidly, but he could not bring himself to take off. His parents tried to encourage him, but he was too scared to listen. On the other hand, his first successful flight was a completely different experience. He was no longer afraid. He felt the wind in his wings and the sun on his face. He soared through the air with confidence and joy. He had finally overcome his fear and achieved his dream of flying. The contrast between the young seagull’s initial attempts to fly and his first successful flight is a testament to the power of determination and perseverance. When the young seagull was afraid, he could not fly. But when he overcame his fear, he was able to achieve anything he set his mind to. The story of the young seagull is a reminder that we all have the potential to achieve our dreams, no matter how difficult they may seem. All we need is the courage to face our fears and the determination to keep trying.

items.stem: “I’ll take the risk.” What is the risk ? Why does the narrator take it ?
items.answer: The narrator who is the pilot of Dakota plane was flying from Paris to London. He was dreaming to enjoy the weekend holidays with his family. items.stem: You have been asked to present an evaluation of the approaches of both, the Baby Seagull and the Pilot who was lost in the clouds, towards achieving their dreams of conquering the skies. Write this presentation draft including your insights, comparing the approaches of both. You may begin this way: One acknowledges that both, the Seagull and the Pilot, wanted to .......... however, ..........
items.answer: 2024 One acknowledges that both the Seagull and the Pilot wanted to conquer the skies, yet their approaches were quite different. The Baby Seagull’s story is one of determination, resilience, and unwavering belief in oneself. In stark contrast, the Lost Pilot’s journey towards conquering the skies was fraught with uncertainty, confusion, and a lack of direction. Hunger and survival were the baby seagull’s primary motivators to overcome fear and take the first flight. The seagull was desperately looking for food, so it had to take a risk despite its initial hesitation and fear. On the other hand, the pilot faced a different challenge in the form of a storm when he realised that he had gotten lost. He decided to put his trust in a mysterious black aeroplane and follow it like a child. We can learn courage and tenacity from both stories. The pilot took a leap of faith to follow the unknown black aeroplane in the face of difficulty, whereas the seagull flew out of instinctual need. In conclusion, the journeys of the Baby Seagull and the Lost Pilot offer valuable insights into the importance of determination, resilience, and preparation in achieving one’s dreams. While the Baby Seagull’s disciplined approach led to eventual success, the Lost Pilot’s impulsive actions serve as a cautionary tale of the dangers of recklessness and overconfidence. Ultimately, it is the combination of passion, perseverance, and careful planning that paves the way for success in conquering the skies and beyond.
